---
title: "Methods"
subtitle: "How pieces are placed and how to read the result"
---

## Input model

The converter SVG is the geometric source. The nester reads each editable piece group and treats
its cut outline as one rigid polygon. Fold lines, labels, piece IDs, and material assignments stay
attached to that polygon. Hidden source and review layers are ignored. The YAML manifest maps
source pages to cardstock materials; the inventory JSON describes the physical sheets available
for each material.

## Placement search

The program searches placements in descending piece-size order. For each piece it tries allowed
rotations using the configured angular step, then tests candidate positions against the usable
sheet bounds and the requested gap from already placed polygons. It ranks feasible choices using
sheet usage and placement quality, then continues through the remaining pieces. A fixed search
order makes a given input repeatable.

This is a heuristic search over a difficult geometric packing problem. It finds practical layouts
quickly but does not certify a global minimum in sheet count or tool travel. Finer rotation steps
can explore more orientations at additional computation cost.

## Inventory and fallback

Every inventory row has a material, width, height, and quantity. The optimizer can use mixed sheet
sizes for one color and will not create unlimited stock. When it cannot fit all pieces into that
inventory, it falls back to the source PDF page arrangement as a valid comparison layout. The
command output identifies this fallback, so it is not mistaken for a successful optimized pack.

## Reported measures

- **Sheet utilization** is the area of placed piece polygons divided by the sheet area.
- **Estimated inter-piece travel** uses a nearest-neighbor order over piece start points; it is a
  rough reposition estimate, not a simulated cutter path.
- **Minimum gap** is the requested clearance between neighboring piece polygons.

The output master is assembled from the original SVG piece groups transformed onto their assigned
sheet pages. This preserves piece geometry and annotations instead of redrawing the pattern. The
current mode keeps complete outlines apart and does not trim glue tabs.
